map.Lessons 6-13, 6-7 & 6-12 — break numbers: Lessons 6-13, 6-7 & 6-12. Break numbers into prime gears. Mesh them with the greatest common factor. Time them with the least common multiple. Four reader gates stand between a jammed engine and a city that needs it.
map.Previously: Axiom City runs on the Patte: Before: Axiom City runs on the Pattern Engine. It is a tower of gears that turns on whole-number rules. Tonight, gear 12 and gear 18 stopped meshing. The city lights flicker.
map.Previously: the team mapped every street: Before: the team mapped every street of Axiom City onto the Engine's number-grid. Now the core gears are stuck. Only the math that built them can start them again.
map.The core gears jammed — twelve teeth gri: The core gears jammed. Twelve teeth grind on eighteen. I'm the keeper tonight. Nothing turns until we know what these gears are MADE of.
map.Made of? Just hit the override and FORCE: Made of? Just hit the override and FORCE it, kid! Who has time to take a machine apart?
map.Force snaps teeth. We do it right: every: Force snaps teeth. We do it right. Every gear breaks into prime parts, the atoms of the Engine. Find those, and the gears show us how to fit.
map.The Factor Forge — where the keepers spl: The Factor Forge. Here the keepers split any number into its primes.
map.Watch: 36 splits into 4 and 9. Neither i: Watch: 36 splits into 4 and 9. Neither is prime, so I keep splitting. 4 = 2×2, 9 = 3×3. The teal circles are the primes.
map.Definitions, keepers: a prime number has: Words, keepers: a prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11…). A factor tree keeps splitting until every branch ends on a prime. Those primes are the prime factorization.
map.To find a number's prime factorization,: To find a prime factorization, build a factor tree. Split into any two factors. Keep splitting the ones that are not prime. Stop when every branch is a prime number. So 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.
map.Your turn, reader — two gears, two trees: Your turn, reader. Two gears, two trees. Take each one all the way down to primes.
map.The Engine only accepts PRIME gears. Bre: The Engine takes only PRIME gears. Break each number all the way down. Pick the factor tree that ends with only prime numbers.
map.Core gear — the prime factorization of 3: Core gear: the prime factorization of 36:
map.Drive gear — the prime factorization of: Drive gear: the prime factorization of 60:
map.Conceptual: a prime number has exactly t: Conceptual: a prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11…). Keep splitting until every branch ends on a prime.
map.Procedural: split off a factor, then spl: Procedural: split off a factor. Then split any piece that is not prime. 36 → 4 × 9 → (2×2) × (3×3). Stop only when every factor is prime.
map.Gear 24 and gear 36 only mesh on teeth t: Gear 24 and gear 36 mesh only on teeth they SHARE. A shared gear that is too big won't fit. One too small wastes power. We need the GREATEST one that fits both.
map.A factor divides a number evenly. List t: A factor divides a number evenly. List the factors both gears share…
map.…and the biggest shared one is the great: …and the biggest shared one is the greatest common factor.
map.A factor divides a number evenly. The gr: A factor divides a number evenly. The greatest common factor (GCF) is the largest factor two numbers share. Fast way: factor both into primes. Multiply the primes they have in common. 24 & 36 share 2×2×3 = 12.
map.Reader — find the greatest gear that mes: Reader, find the greatest gear that meshes each pair. The Mesh Lock won't open for a smaller one.
map.Two gears mesh only on the teeth they SH: Two gears mesh only on the teeth they SHARE. Find the greatest common factor, the largest gear that fits both. GCF(24, 36) and GCF(18, 30).
map.Conceptual: the GCF is the largest numbe: Conceptual: the GCF is the largest number that divides into BOTH. It is never bigger than the smaller number.
map.Procedural: factor each, then multiply t: Procedural: factor each. Then multiply the primes they share. 24 = 2×2×2×3 and 36 = 2×2×3×3 share 2×2×3 = 12. 18 = 2×3×3 and 30 = 2×3×5 share 2×3 = 6.
map.The timing ring. Two gears start tooth-t: The timing ring. Two gears start tooth to tooth, then spin. The Engine won't fire until they line up again.
map.Gear 6 and gear 8 click back to their st: Gear 6 and gear 8 click back to the start only after a whole number of teeth pass on BOTH. How many teeth until they line up?
map.A multiple is what you get counting by a: A multiple is what you get counting by a number: 6, 12, 18, 24… The least common multiple is the first number in BOTH gears' lists. It is never smaller than the larger gear.
map.A multiple of a number is that number ti: A multiple of a number is that number times 1, 2, 3… The least common multiple (LCM) is the smallest multiple two numbers share. Fast way: factor both. Take each prime the most times it appears. 6 & 8 → 2×2×2×3 = 24.
map.Run the rings, reader — find the fewest: Run the rings, reader. Find the fewest teeth until each pair lines up again.
map.Two gears start aligned, then spin. They: Two gears start lined up, then spin. They line up again at their least common multiple. LCM(6, 8) and LCM(4, 10). How many teeth until each pair lines up again?
map.Conceptual: a common multiple sits in BO: Conceptual: a common multiple is in BOTH counting lists. The LEAST common multiple is the smallest one. It is never smaller than the larger number.
map.Procedural: factor each, then take every: Procedural: factor each. Then take every prime the MOST times it appears. 6 = 2×3 and 8 = 2×2×2 → 2×2×2×3 = 24. 4 = 2×2 and 10 = 2×5 → 2×2×5 = 20.
map.Late shift. The core gears are nearly re: Late shift. The core gears are almost ready. Bram finds the override lever.
map.Twelve times eighteen — TWO HUNDRED SIXT: Twelve times eighteen: TWO HUNDRED SIXTEEN turns and they'll line up! I'll spin it that far and FORCE the start!
map.216 is WAY too far — you'll grind the te: 216 is WAY too far. You'll grind the teeth to dust first. These gears share parts. They line up much sooner.
map.Distortion spike. 12 × 18 is A common mu: Distortion spike. 12 × 18 is A common multiple, not the LEAST. The gears share a factor. Ignore it and you go too far. Find the real one before he strips the Engine.
map.Three locks to restart: the greatest gea: Three locks to restart: the greatest gear that meshes them, the fewest teeth until they line up, and what Bram got wrong.
map.The gears are honest. The override isn't: The gears are honest. The override isn't. Reader, take the boss.
Boss Gate: the core gears are 12 and 18. Find their GCF and their LCM. Then name the flaw in Bram's "216 turns."
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. Mesh the gears,: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Mesh the gears, time the gears, and expose the override lie.
map.The master gears have 12 teeth and 18 te: The master gears have 12 teeth and 18 teeth. To restart the Engine, set both dials. Bram is already yanking the override lever. Three locks:

map.Bram yells \"the gears realign after 12: Bram yells "the gears line up after 12 × 18 = 216 turns!" What is his error?
map.Conceptual: the GCF is the largest gear: Conceptual: the GCF is the largest gear that fits both (≤ the smaller). The LCM is the fewest teeth until they line up (≥ the larger).
map.Gear 6 meshes them, realign at 36 — and: Gear 6 meshes them, they line up at 36, and the Engine starts on the FIRST try. No forcing. The city lights are back, steady and bright.
map.Thirty-six?! Not… two hundred sixteen? F: Thirty-six?! Not… two hundred sixteen? Fine. Next time I'll read the gears before I yank a lever.
map.The Engine runs on whole gears — but the: The Engine runs on whole gears, but the city pays in decimals. To be continued…
map.Break it down.Every whole number is buil: Break it down.Every whole number is built from primes. A factor tree splits it until every branch is prime. 36 = 2×2×3×3.
map.Mesh it.The greatest common factor is th: Mesh it.The greatest common factor is the largest gear two numbers share. Multiply the primes they have in common. GCF(24, 36) = 12.
map.Time it.The least common multiple is the: Time it.The least common multiple is the first multiple they share. Take each prime the most times it appears. LCM(6, 8) = 24. It is never smaller than the larger number.
map.The override trap.GCF is small (it fits: The override trap.GCF is small (it fits inside both). LCM is large (both fit inside it). Bram multiplied 12×18 = 216 and ignored the factor of 6 the gears share. The real line-up was 36.
map.\"A number you can't take apart, you don: "If you can't take a number apart, you don't really know it. Find its primes, and the machine is no mystery." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 1 · Episode 3: The Patter: completed Unit 1 · Episode 3: The Pattern Engine. They showed mastery of prime factorization, greatest common factor, and least common multiple.

map.Different number: build the factor tree: A new number: build the factor tree for 18.
map.18 splits into 2 × 9. The 2 is prime — c: 18 splits into 2 × 9. The 2 is prime, so circle it. 9 is not prime, so split again: 9 = 3 × 3.
map.Bottom of the tree: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 — all: Bottom of the tree: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3, all primes. Read the circled numbers.
A new pair: the GCF of 8 and 12.
Prime factors: 8 = 2×2×2 and 12 = 2×2×3. Circle what they SHARE: two 2's.
map.What is the GCF of 10 and 15?: What is the GCF of 10 and 15?
A new pair: the LCM of 4 and 6.
map.4 = 2×2 and 6 = 2×3. Take each prime the: 4 = 2×2 and 6 = 2×3. Take each prime the most times it shows up: 2×2 (from 4) and 3 (from 6).
map.Multiply: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. LCM(4, 6) = 12: Multiply: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. LCM(4, 6) = 12. And 12 is in both lists (4, 8, 12 / 6, 12).
map.What is the LCM of 3 and 5?: What is the LCM of 3 and 5?
map.Check: GCF × LCM = 4 × 40 = 160, and 8 ×: Check: GCF × LCM = 4 × 40 = 160, and 8 × 20 = 160. They always multiply back to the product.
map.Two numbers have a GCF of 3 and a produc: Two numbers have a GCF of 3 and a product of 90. What is their LCM?
Pick one tree for EACH gear, then check.
map.4 × 9 does multiply to 36, but 4 and 9 a: 4 × 9 does multiply to 36, but 4 and 9 are NOT prime. Your tree stopped too soon. Split 4 = 2×2 and 9 = 3×3.
map.6 is not prime — it still splits into 2: 6 is not prime. It still splits into 2 × 3. Keep going until every branch is prime.
map.9 is not prime — split it into 3 × 3. A: 9 is not prime. Split it into 3 × 3. A prime tree has no composite numbers left at the bottom.
map.4 × 15 equals 60, but neither 4 nor 15 i: 4 × 15 equals 60, but 4 and 15 are not prime. Split both: 4 = 2×2 and 15 = 3×5.
map.30 is not prime — that's just the first: 30 is not prime. That is just the first split. Keep going: 30 = 2×3×5.
map.10 is not prime — split it into 2 × 5. E: 10 is not prime. Split it into 2 × 5. Every factor at the bottom must be prime.
map.36 = 2×2×3×3 and 60 = 2×2×3×5 — pure pri: 36 = 2×2×3×3 and 60 = 2×2×3×5. Pure prime gears. The Forge takes them.
12 meshes 24 and 36. 6 meshes 18 and 30. Largest shared gears locked in.
map.72 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 24 an: 72 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 24 and 36, the smallest number they both divide into. The GCF is the largest number that divides into BOTH, so it must be ≤ 24.
map.6 divides both 24 and 36, but it isn't t: 6 divides both 24 and 36, but it isn't the GREATEST. 12 does too. Multiply ALL the shared primes (2×2×3), not just some.
map.4 divides 24 and 36, but you missed the: 4 divides 24 and 36, but you missed the shared 3. The shared primes are 2×2×3 = 12.
map.90 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 18 an: 90 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 18 and 30, not the GCF. The greatest common factor is smaller than both numbers.
map.That divides both, but it isn't the grea: That divides both, but it isn't the greatest. 18 and 30 share 2 AND 3. Multiply them: 2×3 = 6.
map.First box: list the primes 24 and 36 sha: First box: list the primes 24 and 36 share. Multiply them: 2×2×3.
map.Second box: 18 and 30 share 2 and 3. Mul: Second box: 18 and 30 share 2 and 3. Multiply the shared primes.
map.24 teeth and 20 teeth — the gears click: 24 teeth and 20 teeth. The gears click back into place. Cycles synced.
map.48 is just 6 × 8. That's a common multip: 48 is just 6 × 8. That is a common multiple, but not the LEAST. The gears share a factor of 2, so divide it out: 48 ÷ 2 = 24.
map.2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 6 and: 2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 6 and 8, not the LCM. The least common multiple is the smallest number BOTH divide into, so it must be ≥ 8.
map.6 divides 12, but 8 does not. The LCM mu: 6 divides 12, but 8 does not. The LCM must be in BOTH lists. Keep going to 24.
map.40 is just 4 × 10. They share a factor o: 40 is just 4 × 10. They share a factor of 2. Divide it out: 40 ÷ 2 = 20.
map.2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 4 and: 2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 4 and 10, not the LCM. The LCM must be ≥ 10.
map.First pair: take 2 the most times it app: First pair: take 2 the most times it appears (three times, from 8). Times 3 → 24.
map.Lock 1 wants the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR,: Lock 1 wants the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR, but 36 is the LCM. You swapped them. The GCF is the largest gear that fits BOTH, so it is ≤ 12.
map.Lock 1 holds. 12 = 2×2×3 and 18 = 2×3×3: Lock 1 holds. 12 = 2×2×3 and 18 = 2×3×3 share 2×3. Multiply the shared primes.
map.Lock 2 wants the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE,: Lock 2 wants the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE, but 6 is the GCF. Swapped again. The LCM is the fewest teeth until they line up, so it is ≥ 18.
map.Lock 2 holds, but 216 = 12 × 18 isn't th: Lock 2 holds, but 216 = 12 × 18 isn't the LEAST. Divide out the shared factor 6: 216 ÷ 6 = 36.
map.Lock 2 holds. Take each prime the most i: Lock 2 holds. Take each prime the most times it appears: 2×2×3×3 = 36.
map.Lock 3 holds. Multiplying isn't the slip: Lock 3 holds. Multiplying is not the slip by itself. The problem is the NUMBER he gets. Compare 216 to the real LCM.
map.Lock 3 holds. Realignment really is abou: Lock 3 holds. Lining up really is about a MULTIPLE, not the GCF. But his multiple is too big. Why?
map.Lock 3 holds. The gears share a factor o: Lock 3 holds. The gears share a factor of 6, so they line up at 36, not 216. Pick what went wrong.
Lock 3 holds. Name Bram's exact slip.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. GCF 6, LCM 36 — and Bram: ALL LOCKS OPEN. GCF 6, LCM 36. Bram's 216 ignored the factor of 6 the gears share. The Pattern Engine roars back to life.
